message.content:
Since the number has remainder \(10\) when divided by both \(11\) and \(13\), we have

\[
n \equiv 10 \pmod{11}, \qquad n \equiv 10 \pmod{13}.
\]

Because \(11\) and \(13\) are relatively prime,

\[
n \equiv 10 \pmod{143}.
\]

So write

\[
n = 10 + 143k.
\]

We also need

\[
n \equiv 5 \pmod{7}.
\]

Now \(143 \equiv 3 \pmod{7}\), so

\[
10 + 143k \equiv 3 + 3k \pmod{7}.
\]

We need

\[
3 + 3k \equiv 5 \pmod{7}
\]

\[
3k \equiv 2 \pmod{7}.
\]

Since \(3^{-1} \equiv 5 \pmod{7}\),

\[
k \equiv 10 \equiv 3 \pmod{7}.
\]

Thus

\[
k = 3 + 7m.
\]

Then

\[
n = 10 + 143(3 + 7m) = 439 + 1001m.
\]

We need the largest \(n < 2010\):

\[
439 + 1001m < 2010
\]

\[
1001m < 1571.
\]

The largest integer \(m\) is \(1\), giving

\[
n = 439 + 1001 = 1440.
\]

The answer is \(\boxed{1440}\).
